item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Thu Oct 15 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Thu Oct 15 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Thu Oct 15 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.description: The Grunwald Gallery of Art at Indiana University Bloomington partners with Surface Design Association to present "Future Tense 2026"-a national student exhibition juried by José Santiago Pérez. item.title: Meet the Author: Winnifred Sullivan — Thu Oct 15, 4:00 PM — ids@iu.edu
item.description: Making a King: The Political Theology of Joan of Arc The College Arts \+ Humanities Institute and the Center for Religion & The Human present a Meet the Author talk with Winnifred Sullivan \(emeritus, Religious Studies\) in conversation with Spencer Dew \(Ohio State University\) about Sullivan's recent book, Making a King: The Political Theology of Joan of Arc \(Columbia, 2026\). Please join us for a reception following the discussion. Winni Sullivan, who has written extensively about the contradictions and paradoxes of religious freedom law in the US, has written a new book about Joan of Arc. Growing out of her teaching at IU and elsewhere, Sullivan presents a young woman of intelligence and courage who thought the religion and politics of her time differently, offering a model, perhaps, of vernacular political theology, a politics of peace free of aristocratic absolutism and greed. item.title: Brown County Art Guild 2026 Annual Raffle — Fri Oct 16, 8:00 AM — Brown County Art Guild
item.description: Take a chance to win ‘Painters Point’, a beautiful original oil painting generously donated by Guild Artist, Allen Hutton. He strives to render the fleeting patterns of light and shadow with the simple purpose of preserving the reality of a landscape at a particular moment in time and season. Allen has achieved numerous awards and his art can be found in both private and corporate collections across the county. Tickets: 1 for $30, 2 for $50, or 5 for $100 Your generosity helps the Guild to preserve its historic collection, promote its award-winning artist members, and offer workshops and programs throughout the year! The drawing of the winning raffle ticket will be held at 3pm on Saturday, November 21, 2026, at the Guild. The winner need not be present for the drawing. Purchase options: In person at the Guild, call 812-988-6185 or purchase raffle tickets at: https://browncountyartguild.org/product/brown-county-art-guild-annual-raffle/ ——————————————————————————————————

item.title: Mamma Mania! – NYC’s Ultimate ABBA Tribute — Fri Oct 16, 7:30 PM — South Van Buren Street
item.description: Prepare to be transported back to the vibrant 1970s with 2025’s #1 booked ABBA Tribute! Mamma Mania! brings the classic hits of one of pop music’s most iconic groups to life. With their dazzling costumes, flawless harmonies, and captivating stage presence, this tribute captures the essence of ABBA’s unforgettable sound. From “Dancing Queen” to “Mamma Mia,” fans will enjoy a night filled with nostalgia from a stellar cast of musicians! item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Sat Oct 17 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Sat Oct 17 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Sat Oct 17 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery.
